about: What the module costs a real table, measured by game.drpg.perf() and audit/live/perf-baseline.mjs in a browser drawing on real hardware. Nothing measured headless goes in runs (CLAUDE.md: perf() at the table is the only place that number is real). E30 opens it with the 1.2.56 baseline, not yet measured; E33 adds a run after E29; E53 compares.

baseline.world: a copy of the table's world that no release with a new migration clause or a GM-store move has opened (before E04, 1.2.63, at the latest)
baseline.hardware: a laptop at 1366x768 whose browser draws on its GPU
baseline.scene: the largest isometric scene in that world

perfFunction.bodyIs: the text from the line `export async function perfReport(` through its closing `}` and that line's newline: diagnostics.mjs:1381-1514 at v1.2.56, 1401-1534 at e4724f5 (134 lines both)
measures: screen: innerWidth x innerHeight (the viewport, not the screen) and devicePixelRatio
asIs: ms per requestAnimationFrame averaged over 60 frames, as the page stands
pulseHeld, pulseCost: the same with body.drpg-no-pulse; Stained Glass only
blurHeld, blurCost: the same with body.drpg-no-blur; Stained Glass only
windowOpen: a bare .drpg-panel probe 460x320 appended, two frames waited; the 4th of six sorted readings
glassRecut: mean of ten drpgGlassRebuild(); Stained Glass only
roomOfActor, othersInRoom: ms per call, 200 calls after one warm call, on the first character
sideEffects: report() whispers the text to the caller (toChat defaults to true): a ChatMessage in the world, so perf() is never run on the campaign world
body classes drpg-no-pulse and drpg-no-blur are toggled for the length of each reading
perfFunction.knownBias: five MutationObservers watch the body's class (selection.mjs, glass.mjs, fog.mjs, own-ring.mjs, remnant-ring.mjs), so the pulse and blur costs include their one-off reactions (U03-diag-a11y-chrome-32); E53's perf() that discards a warm-up is a different method and is recorded as one

revisions.bodyIs: the text from the line `export async function perfReport(` through its closing `}` and that line's newline: diagnostics.mjs:1469-1634 at E33 C13 (166 lines; 134 at v1.2.56)
revisions.change: the lines measured before are measured by the same code, one block appended: "Rolls the GM drew" - two lines read off what the browser kept of the last fifty draws it took part in (roll-draw.mjs drawTimings; the owner's Q3 (a) of 05.10.2026), the drawing GM's packet in to answer out and the roller's asked to dice shown, each a count, a median, the slowest and the step on the way, or "none since this browser loaded"
measures: drewCount, drewMedian, drewSlowest, drewWritten: rolls this browser drew as the GM - how many of the last fifty, the median and the slowest ms from the packet's arrival (drawOnGm) to its answer, and the median ms at which the message was written

drawnCount, drawnMedian, drawnSlowest, drawnAnswered: rolls drawn for this browser as a roller - the same from the request sent (drawAndPlay) to the dice shown, and the median ms at which the answer arrived
revisions.headless: a count and the marks' order are asserted headless (tier 2 "perf() reports the round trip of a roll the GM drew", 13-murder-signals); the milliseconds are the harness's and go nowhere
revisions.liveRun: LIVE-E33-05 at the owner's table: the first run from this body, a player's browser and the GM's each read

headless.verdict: no line of perf() is a table number headless

why.asIs: with pretendToBeVisual, rAF ran at 16.48 ms a frame over 60 frames with nothing painted: a timer
why.pulseCost, blurCost: about 0 by construction: CSS is never drawn
why.glassRecut: getBoundingClientRect is all zeros, so the recut cuts an empty screen
why.roomOfActor, othersInRoom: V8 in Node over the harness world (5 tokens, 6 regions); R10 guards them with a 2.0 ms ceiling, an order-of-magnitude guard, not the table's number
why.headless Chromium: software compositing: perfReport's own comment has 150 ms a frame against 16.7 for the blur alone in the glass harness
why.drewMedian, drawnMedian: jsdom clients in one process on one machine, the GM's judgement included: a round trip with no network in it

worldCopy.why: Not recorded before 1.2.63 shipped (26.09.2026). The owner updates by hand and copies the world before installing 1.2.63, so an unmigrated copy should exist on the owner's machine, but it is not in DRPG_FIXTURES and its manifest was never taken, so this repository cannot name it. `node audit/live/world-manifest.mjs <that copy> --write` records it as taken.
